blocks.title: Chromatogram and locating agent
blocks.text: Once the paper is dried, the pattern on it is the chromatogram. Coloured components can be identified visually; if they are colourless the chromatogram must be developed by chemical or physical techniques. A locating agent is a chemical that reacts with colourless substances, such as amino acids, to give coloured products visible for inspection.
A convenient way to visualise a colourless chromatogram is to view it under a UV lamp, where the spots appear coloured. Alternatively a locating agent such as ninhydrin is used to locate the spots.

blocks.prompt: What is meant by developing a chromatogram, and what is a locating agent used for (exercise Q.2h; MCQ IX)?
blocks.explanation: Developing means treating the dried paper so that invisible, colourless spots can be seen, either by viewing under ultraviolet light or by spraying a locating agent. A locating agent such as ninhydrin reacts with the colourless components, for example amino acids, to give coloured products that mark their positions.

items: Chromatogram = the dried pattern; colourless spots are shown under a UV lamp or with a locating agent such as ninhydrin (coloured products with amino acids).
